title: The social surface mounts in a fake reader page and every R6 page loads and deep-links under /social

tasks.title: Surface entry, host-bridged router, the routes of R6 and social's not-found page
Surface library build with the release manifest
Harness page, harness journeys and the L3 and L4a CI lanes

acs.text: WHEN the surface is built THE SYSTEM SHALL emit an ES module entry whose default export is the Surface, its chunks, exactly one CSS file and a `manifest.json` that the reader's pinned manifest schema accepts, listing every chunk and the stylesheet with a matching sha384 integrity hash; and the build SHALL fail if surface code imports `@tanstack/react-start` or `app/src/server`.
scenarios: The surface build is loadable by the reader

acs.text: WHEN the surface router changes page THE SYSTEM SHALL do it through `host.navigate` (push or replace) and build hrefs with `host.href`, and WHEN the reader's location changes (Back, Forward) THE SYSTEM SHALL render the page for the new location without navigating again (R4).
scenarios: Navigation goes through the host and Back comes from the reader

acs.text: WHEN the surface is mounted on `/social`, `/social/r/$roomId`, `/social/s/$shiurId` or `/social/settings` with no prior navigation (a deep link) THE SYSTEM SHALL render that page, and WHEN it is mounted on any other path under `/social`, or with an id that does not match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,128}$`, THE SYSTEM SHALL render social's own not-found page (R6).
scenarios: Deep links and social's not-found page

acs.text: WHEN a social page has search parameters THE SYSTEM SHALL validate them per route, drop unknown ones, and write them in the reader's plain `k=v` format (R7).
scenarios: Search parameters are validated per route

acs.text: WHEN social navigates THE SYSTEM SHALL leave `window.history` and `window.location` untouched (R1).
scenarios: Social never touches the browser history

acs.text: WHEN social renders a link THE SYSTEM SHALL render a real `<a href>` built by the host and hand a plain click to the host; a link to a ref SHALL take its href from the reader's workspace commands and navigate with `commands.go` (R15).
scenarios: Links are real hrefs handed to the host

acs.text: WHEN the persistent mount runs and the reader's address has no social `ctx` THE SYSTEM SHALL render nothing, and with `ctx=social.room.<id>` it SHALL render a link to that room's page; WHEN a second page mount starts THE SYSTEM SHALL unmount the first (R18).
scenarios: The persistent mount renders only inside a social context

acs.text: WHEN the Start app's route tree and the surface's route tree are compared THE SYSTEM SHALL find the same five paths, all under `/social` (R2).
WHEN the Start app runs standalone THE SYSTEM SHALL serve the same routes under the browser's own history (R5).
scenarios: Standalone mode uses the browser history

acs.text: WHEN the host is another contract major or lacks members THE SYSTEM SHALL render a "please reload" notice and report `contract-mismatch` instead of mounting.
scenarios: A host from another major gets the reload notice

acs.text: WHEN the built surface is loaded into the harness through its manifest, on a desktop and a phone viewport, in English and Hebrew THE SYSTEM SHALL load every R6 page from a deep link with `lang`/`dir` for the interface language, move through pages with the browser's Back and Forward, and show the persistent mount's way back into a room from a reader page in a social context.
WHEN `/social/r/$roomId` opens with a valid id THE SYSTEM SHALL show the room lobby placeholder naming that room id.
scenarios: The room lobby names its room

acs.text: WHEN `/social/s/$shiurId` opens with a valid id THE SYSTEM SHALL show the shiur placeholder naming that shiur id.
scenarios: The shiur page names its shiur
